chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bought the straw of a stack before it was trodden down, [buying] the straw of every stack for a known amount, taking the straw and selling it before the grain is measured. He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible
key_terms.يُدَاس: Treaded down (to separate grain from straw)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy straw from a grain stack before it is separated and measured?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurara, clarifies that pre-harvest sale of straw is permissible provided the price is fixed and the transaction precedes the final measurement of the grain, thereby mitigating *gharar* (uncertainty). It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between permissible conditional sales and those invalidated by excessive ambiguity regarding quantity or quality, a key topic in the Chapter of *Gharar*.
